name: K'ap Shap
description: K'ap Shap (also known as 'Collecting Tens' or 'Ten-Step') is a traditional Chinese rummy-style game played with Chinese dominoes. The name translates to 'to complete tens,' reflecting the core mechanic: forming pairs that sum to 10 or 20. It is a fast-paced game of matching and drawing, often played as a fast-turnaround gambling game in social clubs.
deck: One or more sets of Chinese Dominoes (32 tiles per set)

history.origins: Originating in Southern China (Cantonese culture), K'ap Shap is one of the most popular social domino games. It occupies a similar cultural space to Gin Rummy in the West.
timeline: 1900s: Follows the Chinese diaspora to San Francisco, Malaysia, and Hong Kong.
Present: A staple in community centers and family gatherings.
history.cultural: Commonly played during New Year celebrations for small-stakes betting.
history.evolution: The game's rules for 'Supreme' tiles (4-2 counting as 3 instead of 6) developed to maintain the 'Tens' theme.

setup.deck: 32 Chinese domino tiles (Civil and Military pairs).
setup.dealing: First player gets 10 tiles, others get 9. Tiles are shuffled face-down and stacked in a wall.

rules.objective: Form a 'Legal Hand' consisting of one identical pair and four additive pairs (totaling 10 or 20).
rules.gameplay:
1. First player discards a tile.
2. Next players can either take the discard (if it completes their winning hand) or draw from the wall.
3. Every turn must end with a discard unless the player declares a win.
keyRules: Winning hand: one identical pair (eye) plus four pairs summing to 10 or 20 pips; the 4-2 tile counts as 3 pips.
First player may discard without drawing; others may take a face-up tile from the table or draw from the wall, then discard one.
Game begins with each player putting an equal ante into the pot; winner collects the pot.

strategy.basic: Prioritize forming the 'Eye' (identical pair) early, as it's the hardest part of the hand to complete. Keep tiles that are versatile for 'Tens' (like 5s and 6s).
strategy.intermediate: Watch for 'Dead Tiles': If three double-six tiles have already been discarded by others, your remaining double-six can never form an Eye and should be used in a total-sum pair instead.
strategy.advanced: The 'Wait Rule': If you draw a tile that *could* complete a 10-sum, but it's a Military tile with no matching partner left in the deck, discard it immediately to avoid 'clogging' your hand.
tips: The four-two tile is the most flexible because its value change (from 6 to 3) allows for unexpected 10-sum completions.
Always verify the number of sets in play; with 4 sets, the probability of finding an identical pair increases significantly.

variations.name: K'ap Shap (two-player)
variations.description: Two-player variant: single set of 32 tiles, wall four high and eight wide. First player takes 8 tiles, second takes 7. Winning hand: one identical pair (eye) plus three pairs summing to 10 or 20 (not four pairs).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant differs in hand size and pair count; engine overrides for initialHandSize and meldConfig could be added when needed.

scoring.description: No points; first player to complete a legal hand wins and collects the ante pot.
scoring.winCondition: First player to complete a legal hand (one identical pair plus four pairs summing to 10 or 20 pips, the 4-2 tile counting as 3) wins and collects the pot.
